parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آفیون (afyon), from Arabic أَفْيُون (ʔafyūn), from Ancient Greek ὄπιον (ópion). Cognate with English opium.

parole.significato: anise, an umbelliferous plant of the species Pimpinella anisum and the liqueur made from its seeds
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آناصون (anason, “anise”), from Old Anatolian Turkish [Term?], from Arabic أَنِيسُون (ʔanīsūn, “anise”), from Ancient Greek ἄνισον (ánison), ultimately from Egyptian jnst.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بلغم (balgam), from Arabic بَلْغَم (balḡam), ultimately from Ancient Greek φλέγμα (phlégma, “phlegm”).

parole.significato: chameleon, a reptile of the family Chamaeleonidae, able to change color and project its long tongue
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بوقلمون (bukalemun), from Arabic أَبُوقَلَمُون (ʔabūqalamūn), ultimately from Ancient Greek ὑποκάλαμον (hupokálamon).

parole.significato: geography (study of physical structure and inhabitants of the Earth)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جغرافیا, from Arabic جُغْرَافِيَا (juḡrāfiyā), from Ancient Greek γεωγραφία (geōgraphía).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish افلاطون (eflatun), from Arabic أَفْلَاطُون (ʔaflāṭūn), from Ancient Greek Πλάτων (Plátōn), with semantic narrowing. Doublet of Eflatun.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فلقه (falaka), from Arabic فَلَقَة (falaqa), ultimately from Ancient Greek φάλαγξ (phálanx).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فانوس (fanus), from Arabic فَانُوس (fānūs), from Ancient Greek φανός (phanós, “lantern”).
From Ottoman Turkish خریطه (harita, harıta), from Arabic خَرِيطَة (ḵarīṭa), from Ancient Greek χάρτης (khártēs).
From Ottoman Turkish اقلیم (iklim), from Arabic إِقْلِيم (ʔiqlīm), from Ancient Greek κλίμα (klíma).

parole.significato: retort, still, alembic, distiller, a flask with a rounded base and a long neck that is bent down and tapered, used to h…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish انبیق (imbik, “retort, still, alembic”), from Arabic إِنْبِيق (ʔinbīq, “alembic”), ultimately from Ancient Greek ἄμβιξ (ámbix, “alembic”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish انجیل (incil), from Arabic إِنْجِيل (ʔinjīl), from Ancient Greek εὐαγγέλιον (euangélion, “good news”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاموس (kamus, “ocean; name of a celebrated Arabic dictionary”), from Arabic قَامُوسٌ (qāmūsun), from Ancient Greek ὠκεανός (ōkeanós). Doublet of okyanus.

parole.significato: law, statute, code, written set of rules
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قانون, from Arabic قَانُون (qānūn) (whence also Persian قانون), from Ancient Greek κανών (kanṓn). Cognate with English canon. Doublet of kanon.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كیمیا (kimiya, kimya), from Arabic كِيمِيَاء (kīmiyāʔ), from Ancient Greek χυμείᾱ (khumeíā).

From kon- (“to be put down”) + -u (deverbal nominal suffix), a calque of Arabic مَوْضُوع (mawḍūʕ, “that which is laid down”), itself a calque of Ancient Greek ὑποκείμενον (hupokeímenon, “that which is laid down”). Coined in 1933 from a suggestion by a member of the public in the newspaper Hakimiyet-

parole.significato: severe pain felt throughout the body, especially in the shoulders
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قولنج (kulunc, “colic; cramp”), from Arabic قَوْلَنْج (qawlanj, “colic, colitis”), ultimately from Ancient Greek κωλικός (kōlikós, “suffering in the colon”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قرطاسيه (kırtasiye), from Arabic قرطاس (qirṭās, “paper”) + -iye (“suffix indicating a place”), ultimately from Ancient Greek χάρτης (khártēs, “papyrus, paper”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لادن, from Arabic لَادَن (lādan, “gum cistus”), from Ancient Greek λᾱ́δᾰνον (lā́dănon).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish منجنیق (mancanık, mancınık), from Arabic مَنْجَنِيق (manjanīq), ultimately from Ancient Greek μαγγανικά (manganiká).

parole.significato: myrtle, an evergreen shrub or small tree of the genus Myrtus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مرسین (mersin, “myrtle”), from Arabic مَرْسِين (marsīn), ultimately from Ancient Greek μυρσίνη (mursínē).

parole.significato: jute mallow, mulukhiyah, any annual herb of the species Corchorus olitorius, used as a vegetable
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ملوخیه (mülhiye, “jute mallow”), from Arabic مُلُوخِيَّة (mulūḵiyya, “jute mallow”), ultimately from the plural form of Ancient Greek μολόχιον (molókhion, “mallow”).
From Ottoman Turkish مقناطس, مقناطیس (mıknatıs), from Arabic مِغْنَاطِيس (miḡnāṭīs), from Ancient Greek μαγνήτης (magnḗtēs, “atrractive”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اقیانوس (okyanus), from Arabic أُوقْيَانُوس (ʔūqyānūs), from Ancient Greek Ὠκεανός (Ōkeanós).
From Arabic سَعْتَر (saʕtar), from Ancient Greek σάτυρος (sáturos). Doublet of satir.

parole.significato: cherry laurel, an evergreen shrub of the species Prunus laurocerasus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طفلان (taflan, “cherry laurel”), from a variant of Arabic دِفْلَى (diflā, “oleander”), ultimately from Ancient Greek δᾰ́φνη (dắphnē, “sweet bay”). Doublet of defne.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طرخون (tarhun), from Arabic طَرْخُون (ṭarḵūn), from Ancient Greek δρακόντιον (drakóntion).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طلسم (tılsım), borrowed from Arabic طِلَسْم (ṭilasm), borrowed from Ancient Greek τέλεσμα (télesma, “payment”), from τελέω (teléō, “to pay”) + -μα (-ma).

parole.significato: astrolabe, an astronomical and navigational instrument for gauging the altitude of the Sun and stars
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسطرلاب (usturlab, “astrolabe”), from Arabic أَسْطُرْلَاب (ʔasṭurlāb), from Ancient Greek ἀστρολάβος (astrolábos).
From Ottoman Turkish زار (zar, “die”), from Arabic زَهْر (zahr, “cube, die”) from Ancient Greek τέσσερα (téssera, “four”) from Ancient Greek τέσσᾰρᾰ (téssără, “four”).
